Where it began

Dan Lawrence was born at Whipps Cross on 12 July 1997 and went to Trinity Catholic High School in Woodford Green. His cricket began at Chingford Cricket Club, where he played his junior cricket. As a boy he tried out all sorts of batting methods, and something of that spirit of invention stayed with him.

Essex gave him his first-class debut in April 2015, against Kent. In only his second match he made a hundred against Surrey, aged 17 years and 290 days, the third youngest to make a County Championship century. At the 2016 Under-19 World Cup his 174 from 150 balls against Fiji set a new best for an England batter in youth one-day internationals.

The player

He helped Essex win promotion and then, in their first season back in the top division, the County Championship in 2017. That year the Cricket Writers' Club named him its young cricketer of the year. Strong form for the England Lions against a Cricket Australia XI early in 2020 put him in the frame for a Test place.

His Test debut came against Sri Lanka in 2021, in the first match of the series, and he made 73 in his first innings. His best score, 91, came in Barbados the following year, when he fell to the last ball of the day. In August 2026 Joe Root, back as captain, brought him back for the first Test against Pakistan, and he made 51 in his first innings. By November 2026 he had played 17 Tests, with 858 runs at 29.59 and seven fifties.

What made him special

He liked to score quickly, as his 218 from 190 balls for Surrey would later show, and he was a handy extra bowler. His off-breaks came from an unusual action, and his first Test wicket was Will Young of New Zealand. He finished with five Test wickets at 30.00.

The one thing missing by November 2026 was a Test hundred. He had made seven fifties, among them a 73 and a 91, so it was clearly not for want of trying. County bowlers would have told England the hundreds were in there somewhere.

Away from the middle

He moved from Essex to Surrey ahead of the 2024 season, and in June 2026 he showed them why. Against Hampshire at The Oval he made 218 from 190 balls, his first double hundred, and then 101 from 64 balls in the second innings. Only one batter before him had made a double hundred and a hundred in the same County Championship match at better than a run a ball.

He also played franchise cricket for London Spirit in The Hundred and for Brisbane Heat and Melbourne Stars in Australia's Big Bash League.

And finally

Sport runs in the family, though not always with a bat. His brother Tom is a professional wrestler, fighting as David Wreckham. Family arguments about who has the tougher job are presumably settled by a quiet word rather than a headlock.
